This is a broad operating leadership role. It combines capital program delivery, construction, network operations, asset performance, service-provider management, technology implementation, financial accountability and Board-level communication. The successful candidate will move Ivy from managing individual projects to managing repeatable programs at scale. Reports to: President Location: Greater Toronto Area; hybrid with regular travel to project sites and partner locations Direct reports: Construction Manager; Operations Manager; operations and program delivery resources Role scope: Capital delivery, network operations, asset performance, vendors, systems and operational excellence What we offer As a growing company in the EV charging sector, Ivy values the experience, judgement and contributions of each team member. The role includes: Competitive executive compensation and benefits. RRSP matching program. Hybrid, GTA-based working model with regular presence at Ivy, Hydro One, partner and project locations. Executive exposure to Ivy’s Board, parent company stakeholders and major customers. The opportunity to help shape a growing Ontario infrastructure platform. Key roles and responsibilities Capital program and delivery Inform and deliver against an approved annual capital budget safely, on time and on budget. Deployment and Delivery program includes charger replacements, site optimization, and large multisite developments with Ivy’s real-estate partners Establish program governance across scope, schedule, cost, quality, safety, risk, change control, procurement interfaces, commissioning and handover. Implement the appropriate delivery model for each portfolio, including qualified-vendor, end-to-end program partner and hybrid approaches. Create transparent reporting that provides management and the Board early visibility into delivery risk, forecast changes and corrective actions. Build future capital plans and recommend delivery capacity, sequencing and resourcing requirements. Network operations and asset performance Own operational performance across uptime, visit success rate, charge success rate, mean time to resolution and site availability. Develop a reliability and lifecycle-management strategy using root-cause analysis, warranty recovery, preventive maintenance, spares readiness and asset-performance data. Establish incident, escalation and restoration processes that prioritize customer impact and minimize avoidable downtime. Partner closely with the commercial and customer teams on service standards, major partner commitments and customer-impacting issues. Service partners and operational systems Build and manage a non-exclusive, multi-vendor O&M model with clear regional coverage, SLAs, scorecards, escalation paths and accountability. Lead the implementation and adoption of Clockwork as the work-order, workflow and operating-insight platform. Integrate internal teams, service providers, OEMs and other partners into consistent intake, dispatch, approval, parts, close-out and reporting workflows. Use automation, analytics and AI-enabled workflows to reduce manual coordination, improve response times and generate actionable operating insights. Financial and executive leadership Manage the capital and operating budgets within approved authorities and provide accurate forecasts. Improve cost discipline using measures such as cost per port installed, cost per kilowatt installed, O&M cost per charger and cost per dispatch. Lead, coach and develop the construction and operations teams and clarify roles as the organization scales. Present operating plans, performance, risks and recommendations to the President, Board and Hydro One stakeholders in a clear executive format. Contribute to enterprise strategy, annual planning, organizational design and cross-functional decision-making. Year-one outcomes Deliver the approved 2027 capital program against planned schedule, budget, safety and quality commitments. Maintain replacement-site capital efficiency against $/port, $/kW and other investment criteria guardrails Improve uptime, visit success rate, charge success rate, and mean time to resolution against agreed targets. Complete ticketing and workflow system implementation, and establish reliable workflow and management reporting. Onboard at least one additional qualified service and maintenance provider and implement vendor scorecards and SLA governance. Establish baseline and improvement plans for O&M cost per charger, cost per dispatch and delivery productivity. Qualifications and experience Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, construction management or a related field; professional designation or equivalent experience is an asset. EV charging experience is valuable but not required; the ability to scale an operating platform is essential. Senior operating leadership experience (10+ years) in infrastructure, utilities, transportation, telecommunications, distributed energy, field services or another asset-intensive environment. Demonstrated accountability for a significant annual capital program and operating budget. Track record delivering multi-site programs through internal teams, EPC partners, contractors, OEMs and field-service providers. Strong understanding of program controls, procurement, construction, commissioning, maintenance, asset management and operational performance. Experience implementing workflow, work-order, asset-management or field-service technology and driving adoption across vendors and teams. Excellent executive communication, financial judgement and Board-level presentation skills. Application process Thank you to all those who apply. However, only candidates considered for an interview will be contacted. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, or disability status. Please submit your application with resume and cover letter by 11:59 PM E.D.T., November 30, 2026 via this job posting on Bamboo. Address your cover letter to Kyle Mersky , President. About Ivy Ivy Charging Network’s mission is to enable electrified journeys right here in Ontario through simple, intuitive and reliable EV charging solutions. We operate one of Ontario’s largest public EV charging networks and are building on that foundation to support a broader range of fleet electrification needs. Our fast-charging network spans major urban hubs and high-speed corridors, including ONroute locations, while our destination chargers provide additional charging options in communities across Ontario. With expanded fleet and facility energy expertise, we also support commercial fleets with charging solutions designed around their operational needs. Wholly owned by Hydro One Limited, Ivy is focused on making EV charging easier and more reliable for the people and businesses we serve. From public charging along Ontario’s busiest routes to charging solutions for commercial fleets, we’re helping keep personal and fleet EV drivers moving. review_candidates.description: Discover Your Career at Emory University Emory University is a leading research university that fosters excellence and attracts world-class talent to innovate today and prepare leaders for the future. We welcome candidates who can contribute to the excellence of our academic community. Description The Carter Center is a 501(c)(3), not-for-profit, nongovernmental organization founded in 1982 in Atlanta, GA, by former U.S. President Jimmy Carter and his wife, Rosalynn, in partnership with Emory University. The Center has helped to improve millions of lives in more than 80 countries by waging peace, fighting disease, and building hope. The Carter Center is guided by a fundamental commitment to human rights and the alleviation of human suffering. It seeks to prevent and resolve conflicts, enhance freedom and democracy, and improve health. The Carter Center collaborates with other organizations, public and private, in carrying out its mission around the world. Current information about the Center’s many programs and activities are available at The Carter Center. SUMMARY: The Carter Center works to prevent, mitigate, and resolve conflicts to build transformative and sustainable peace. The Conflict Resolution Program works toward an inclusive, holistic approach to peacebuilding – one that addresses various dimensions of the conflict – based on the belief that sustainable peace depends on engaging with everyone affected by the decisions made by the people at the peace table. Its gender-conscious approach includes constructive change initiatives that go beyond the resolution of conflicts, reaffirming the importance of women’s participation and involvement at all levels of the peace and security agenda and the development of local solutions to global problems. Under this initiative, the Carter Center currently supports programs in the U.S., the Middle East, and Africa. Program Associate’s scope of work will include but is not limited to support to the current implementation of The Carter Center’s U.S. conflict resolution programming. The Program Associate acts as an integral member of the team to which they are assigned. The Program Associate will help plan, implement, and conduct follow-up, including reporting and evaluation, regarding all events related to the projects to which they have been assigned, including, but not limited to, workshops, conferences, and field visits. Monitors ongoing events developments in U.S. politics, especially those related to political and identity-based violence. Facilitates coordination with other parts of The Carter Center. Assists in drafting project related proposals, reports, memoranda, and public information. Helps drafts and monitor budgets, consultant agreements, and procurement. Supports operations including overseeing logistical planning for events, as well as management of interns and volunteers. This position will report to the Associate Director, Conflict Resolution Program. FORMAL JOB DESCRIPTION: Primary duty is organizing, coordinating, and planning operational facets of a global program and its related activities which include, but are not limited to the following: researching factors that may impact the success of the program, and working with individuals or groups to research and document program requirements in order to provide appropriate input. Monitors and reports progress of objectives and goals of the program. Develops promotional materials/venues, manages relational databases, and establishes/forecasts budget requirements. Develops work plans to accomplish objectives and monitors progress toward their achievement. Monitors expenditures and may prepare financial reports; may assist in identifying funding resources and developing fund-raising strategies and initiatives. Prepares operational and statistical reports to assist in effective decision-making. Conducts training, represents the program at international meetings and conferences, and networks with affiliated groups. May write or develop reports, speeches, briefings, newsletters, promotional materials, grants or other written materials related to the program. Conducts research and gathers accurate information to develop various publications. May plan, administer, or monitor the program's budget or related grants. May assist in developing and coordinating program-related conferences, conventions, or meetings. May supervise staff. Performs related responsibilities as required. This is not an administrative support position. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: Bachelor's degree in a field related to the program and two years of related experience or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: Ability to juggle numerous demands under tight deadlines while keeping a level head and a positive attitude. Highly advanced intercultural and interpersonal skills are key to this position's success. Strong ability to communicate, both orally and in writing, computer skills, and teamwork are a must. Knowledge of domestic U.S. politics, prior experience on political campaigns, experience with strategic communication, as well as monitoring and evaluation highly preferred. Experience in peacebuilding work preferred. NOTE: This role will be granted the opportunity to work from home regularly but must be able to commute to The Carter Center on a flexible weekly schedule based upon business needs. Schedule is based on agreed upon guidelines. All non-exempt employees must reside within the state of Georgia. The Carter Center reserves the right to change remote work status with notice to employee. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States for any employer. You will work directly with development, engineering, procurement, interconnection, permitting, and execution teams to ensure projects are commercially de-risked before reaching NTP. Responsibilities Include Creating and maintaining project-specific CapEx estimates, OpEx forecasts, cost breakdowns, and spend schedules aligned with development and interconnection milestones for assigned Primergy's portfolio of projects. Estimate and schedule updates will be used to support the development, interconnection, engineering, procurement, and construction teams in the development stages prior to NTP. Work with development engineering and development teams in the early stage of a project to help identify and document construction risks and assumptions, tracking them through the development lifecycle to de-risk prior to NTP. During early development, assist the development engineering team in identifying requirements for preliminary geotechnical investigations and pile load testing, offsite access options and constraints, construction water needs and availability, and site constructability concerns to be mitigated or captured in constraints assumptions in the risk registry. Leading the compilation and administration of comprehensive EPC bid packages that include all project-level information, assumptions, and risks to minimize scope gaps, preparing drafts for Director of Preconstruction review. Maintain and coordinate RFI logs tracker during RFP stage by facilitating responses from internal SME’s and disseminating answers to all bidders. Lead compilation of Primergy team analysis of EPC bids and identifying exclusions that could drive pricing increases, including the administration of the negotiation log for each EPC bidder; prepare bid comparison matrices and supporting materials for the Director of Preconstructions recommendations and presentations to leadership on EPC selection and strategy. Maintain the cost database that supports preparation of capex estimates and forecasting of project construction timelines based upon indicative bids, hard bids and subscription sources. During the development phase, prepare comprehensive construction permit lists in conjunction with the developer for each project and help ensure requirements are incorporated into the EPC RFP solicitation and de-risked where critical path to start of construction; flag critical path permits to the Director of Preconstruction. Work cross-functionally with other groups in the organization to support process improvements and boost efficiency. Education And Experience Requirements 10+ years of experience in US power markets, origination, development, strategic Bachelor's degree in engineering, construction management, or related field preferred; equivalent combination of education and experience considered. Minimum of 8 years of experience in the construction or development industry, with a minimum of 4 years specifically in a preconstruction role for utility-scale solar PV and BESS projects. Demonstrated hands-on experience with capex estimating, constructability review, and EPC bid analysis on large scale renewable energy projects. Experience working across the project lifecycle from early-stage development and constructability through EPC RFP, EPC selection, and NTP preparation. Familiarity with construction permitting processes, typical AHJ requirements, and how permit timelines interface with project schedules. Experience working with federal, state, and local agencies; ability to maintain professional relationships with external stakeholders. Skillset Strong quantitative skills; comfortable building and maintaining cost models in Excel. Solid understanding of construction scheduling, critical path methodology, and how schedule assumptions translate to budget risk. Ability to read and interpret civil, structural, electrical, and site design drawings at a level sufficient to identify constructability issues. Clear written and verbal communication; able to translate technical findings into concise summaries for internal stakeholders. Detail-oriented and organized; capable of tracking multiple active projects without losing visibility into any of them. Comfortable operating with a high degree of independence while keeping the Director of Preconstruction informed on material issues. Proficient with Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams); experience with project management tools a plus. Commercial awareness; understands how preconstruction decisions affect project IRR, EPC contract structure, and financing assumptions. Collaborative working style; able to build credibility with engineers, contractors, and project managers across organizational boundaries. Able to work in a remote environment and collaborate with peers through various digital media methods such as MS Teams, Zoom and other Primergy adopted available tools Honesty and integrity; strong personal accountability and ownership of work product. Primergy is committed to cultivating an inclusive and welcoming workplace. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status. We understand that individuals from historically underrepresented groups may hesitate to apply if they don't meet 100% of the listed qualification. If this role aligns with your interests and career goals, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all the criteria. Primergy is a developer, owner, and operator specializing in utility-scale solar PV, battery storage projects across the United States. The company manages a significant portfolio of operational and development-stage projects across major energy markets, including ERCOT, MISO, PJM, CAISO, WECC, and SERC. With a talented team bringing decades of expertise in energy project development, financing, construction, and operations, Primergy leads the industry in delivering innovative and sustainable energy solutions. Primergy is a portfolio company of Quinbrook and is the primary investment platform for Quinbrook’s solar and solar plus energy storage activities in North America.
